newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to raise gasoline price 25 pct -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to raise gasoline price 25 pct -- paper.

text.p: Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera is due to shortly announce a 25 percent increase in domestic gasoline prices, so paving the way for further liberalization of the domestic retail market, local papers reported.

Leading daily El Universal said the average retail price would increase to 69 bolivars ($0.14) per liter from the current 55 bolivars, although high-grade fuels would rise proportionately more than lower quality gasolines.
The report did not provide a time frame, although the increases are considered central to an IMF stand-by agreement signed by Venezuela in April last year to bring fuels up to market clearing levels.
Congress is currently studying a new internal market law that, when implemented, would open Venezuela's currently closed retail market to foreign competition and market prices.

Gasoline price hikes are controversial in Venezuela, where motorists, long accustomed to subsidized prices, still drive gas-guzzlers. Despite a nearly 500 percent gasoline increase last year, mineral water is still more expensive than petrol while milk is nearly four times as costly.
